name: UNetbootin
description: Downloads bootable distro ISOs/kernels over plaintext HTTP (hardcoded http:// mirrors) and writes them straight to bootable USB/HDD with no integrity check. [Opus-verified: CONFIRMED-D]
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Inspected path downloads boot-media content, not an application self-update; no global absence claim follows from this path alone.
limitations: Imported from completed SOURCE-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md; retained snapshot only.
Current releases, canonical provenance, and paths outside inspected behavior are not independently established.

original_evidence.text: | UNetbootin | https://github.com/unetbootin/unetbootin | 48956c8 / 2023-06-28 | N (no self-update) | Y (silent, automatic during normal "create USB" workflow) | Y (downloads and writes bootable OS installer images/kernels to USB/HDD) | **plaintext HTTP** — hardcoded distro download URLs use `http://`, e.g. `http://archive.ubuntu.com/...`, `http://download.fedoraproject.org/...`, `http://download.opensuse.org/...`; QNetworkAccessManager used with no TLS at all on this path | none | none — no checksum/signature verification of downloaded ISO/kernel/initrd found | n/a | `src/unetbootin/distrolst.cpp:63-64` (Ubuntu netinst kernel/initrd over `http://archive.ubuntu.com`); dozens more `http://` distro URLs throughout `distrolst.cpp` (Fedora, openSUSE, Gentoo, etc.); download implementation `src/unetbootin/unetbootin.cpp:2611` `downloadfile()` via `QNetworkAccessManager` has no hash/signature check of the downloaded file before writing it to the boot media — the `.md5`/`.sha1` regexes at lines 50-53 are only file-exclusion patterns for what NOT to copy to the USB, not verification logic. **This is the worst finding in the batch: unauthenticated plaintext-HTTP delivery of a bootable OS installer, silently written to media the user then boots from.** |
